verifiedContracts: The packager requires native original SHA, reconstructed candidate SHA, stock Watchdog path/hash and reviewed contract status before producing a profile.
The runner binds probe success to its unique run GUID, completed exhaustion/teardown status and native return code zero. A stale PID result is rejected.

Exit -1 additionally requires a same-parent observed Watchdog at the expected path, the build-bound contract and fresh per-game-PID logs with ordered #TW#-kp, parsed -kp and process-exit debugger markers. Exception/dump markers reject acceptance.
Required ordered game cleanup markers corroborate main cleanup before the stock command; the recorded protocol does not claim all native destruction or the cleanup function returned.
The emitted profile pins the shutdown contract hash and Watchdog file hash. Existing renderer geometry, guard, canonical approval and fresh-directory checks remain active.
Failure handling restores backed-up files; inert actual-runner fixtures cover interrupted copy, cleanup failure, foreign request, stale result and waiting for another game.
limitations: This is source integration acceptance, not a new runtime pass or deployment authorization. Root must regenerate and validate exact package/profile/static approval dependencies before any authorized test.
The -1 interpretation is exclusive to this reviewed stock Watchdog command protocol, after the completed probe teardown and required log milestones. It is not a general nonzero-exit whitelist.
The stock Watchdog terminates during the native shutdown worker after main cleanup; releases following the command and outer cleanup return are not certified.
Observed child identity and log provenance are operational checks for the controlled isolated test; this review does not establish adversarial operating-system integrity or arbitrary mod safety.
